name: long-horizon-agent-landscape
prompt: Using current public web sources, research the most important developments in long-horizon AI agents and agent observability over the past 12 months. Return five concise findings with dates and source citations, then explain the concrete implications for an open-source, object-storage-native agent history and trace platform. Distinguish verified facts from your inferences and avoid repeating unsupported vendor marketing.

name: gcs-agent-journal-design
prompt: Investigate official Google Cloud documentation and credible engineering sources to answer this design question: which guarantees and failure modes matter for append-only agent history and traces that use Google Cloud Storage as their durable source of truth? Cover conditional creation, consistency, hot-key/request scaling, latency, retries, and cost. End with specific engineering rules and identify anything that still requires our own benchmark. Include source citations.

name: open-source-launch-plan
prompt: Act as a pragmatic open-source launch advisor. Farfield makes object storage the durable source of truth for agent history and execution, and currently has a Go server/CLI plus Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Using current ecosystem evidence, produce a focused seven-day announcement-readiness plan. Prioritize what a developer must be able to try and verify, what should explicitly remain out of scope, and which proof points would make the project credible. Include source citations for current ecosystem claims.
